The company saw a large stock price decline just last week.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Hot on the heels of a monumental share price drop for the company, Intel now faces a class action lawsuit from its own shareholders.

This is according to an alert from law firm Robbins LLP, which recently informed all investors. This suit alleges "Intel misled investors about demand for its products and the Company's future growth potential."

The class action can involve anyone who bought stock between July 23, 2026, and October 29, 2026, known as the "class period".

With the memory crisis in full effect, PC sales are down worldwide (estimated to be 20% down in October), but the lawsuit argues that the PC sales slowdown was "having a materially greater negative impact to Intel’s third quarter 2026 Client Computing and Physical AI Group results than defendants had disclosed to investors."

It also argues Intel's OEM and distribution partners were left with hardware they couldn't sell to consumers due to rising prices, and that positive impacts of Intel business coming from the AI boom were off "more than offset by the negative effects on the Company’s business and financial results resulting from the PC market slowdown and the excess inventory buildup."

The suit also alleges that Intel's reporting of its operations and ability to capitalise on the AI boom "were materially false and misleading when made, and such statements did not accurately reflect Intel’s then-present business and prospects."

With Robbins LLP informing investors of this class action lawsuit, it's possible more could join the claim, and we don't actually know how many are currently in the class action right now. The law firm notes that those who purchased stock in the class period have until January 12, 2027, to join.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

It's important to note that Intel stock prices have dropped significantly, declining by 29% at the end of the last month, and upwards of 40% in the last six months. From $95.53 per share on Wednesday, October 28, to $59.66 per share as of the time of writing, that's a 38% decline. To a shareholder, that is a straight devaluation of however much money they would have put into the company in that period.

Intel has had its fair share of ups and downs over the last few years. With a long history behind it, Intel made a killing in the '90s and '00s, becoming a market leader for CPUs, but unstable chips and underperforming chips marked a downward trend for the company. This is all while TSMC has surpassed it in chip manufacturing and AMD has managed to pull ahead in the gaming CPU market. The decline in PC sales thanks to the memory crisis only made things worse for Team Blue.

Intel doesn't appear down for the count, with it gaining market share from AMD just last week (and its recent handheld chips are excellent). Still, some of Intel's own shareholders alleging they've been misled is certainly not a great look for a company that is still very much on its way back up.

3. Best mid-range: Intel Core Ultra 5 250K Plus

James is a more recent PC gaming convert, often admiring graphics cards, cases, and motherboards from afar. It was not until 2019, after just finishing a degree in law and media, that they decided to throw out the last few years of education, build their PC, and start writing about gaming instead. #3727. The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting a New Game Plus mode in next week's update

A New Game Plus mode is coming to vampiric RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker next week.

Developer Rebel Wolves has now detailed everything coming with The Blood of Dawnwalker's Update 1.2, currently planned to go live sometime next week, and top of the list of changes is a New Game Plus for players who have already rolled credits on the game.

"If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with New Game+," the developer revealed earlier today. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over." Rebel Wolves is upping the level cap to 100 for New Game Plus, which will also have items with updated stats and enemies "balanced and scaled uniformly across all regions."

Elsewhere in Update 1.2, the studio is making tweaks to "enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat," and improving terrain geometry to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration." We'll need to wait for more comprehensive patch notes before finding out which enemies are getting spongier or flimsier, however.

While the incoming patch doesn't seem to be as beefy as the last - the one that added animal petting and an easier Story mode - it'll be a good way to sink your teeth deeper into a game that's already begging to be replayed, thanks to a time management mechanic that can drastically change any given run.

The new game from some former The Witcher 3 veterans came out in September and seems to have been a hit. Eurogamer's The Blood of Dawnwalker review called the game a "familiar dark fantasy adventure, but one with bold and provocative ideas of its own, that's mostly, enormously successful."

Despite its mixed reception, Marvel's Wolverine was September's top-selling new game in the US, making Sony launch revenues it hasn't seen since Helldivers 2

#3726. Microsoft Says Of The Next Xbox: ‘Helix Is A Console Capable Of Playing PC Games’

Microsoft has put out an online magazine to celebrate 25 years of Xbox, and unquestionably to attempt even more damage control after a gruesome year of studio closures and mass layoffs. Within all the huff and puff lies a surprise: seven pages’ coverage of Project Helix, the codename for the next Xbox console. Within this is revealed the plan for Helix to be able to play games and even progress from every previous Xbox generation, as well as removing “the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games.” So, asks the magazine and indeed us, “is Project Helix a console or a PC?” The answer is very definitively: a console. Sort of.

The current generation of consoles were notably described ahead of launch as being far more like PCs in a sealed box than the traditional console designs of yore, and this appears to be something Microsoft is looking to get away from this time out. The emphasis here is on the so-called instantaneous nature of a console. Jason Ronald is Xbox’s VP of “next generation,” and is quoted saying, “When I think about what makes a console magical, it’s that it just makes my games instantly accessible and ready to play in an instant. I don’t have to worry about updating my operating system, updating drivers, configuring different settings.” Which is…a bold claim, given anyone who owns an Xbox will know about having to install the latest updates, waiting for game patches to excruciatingly slowly download without taking advantage of your 1TB ethernet connection, or that unbearable pause each time you load it up for it to fill in the dashboard.

But of Project Helix, Ronald says, “it’s really designed to be the ultimate gaming machineâone that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I’m able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly,” adding, “We’re very clear on the design goal: Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games.”

However, it’s hard to know just how clear this distinction is from Ronald’s very next words. “But if you’re a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it.” So it is a PC then? So confused.

Other comments from Ronald include that “We don’t think the next generation is defined by 8K or 240 hertz, or some of the traditional metricsâit’s really about gameplay innovation.” He adds, “It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering, to deliver a new level of visual fidelity in more efficient and innovative ways.” Which all rather seems to be laying the ground for a machine that’s not focusing on the very latest and most expensive chipsets, but rather one that’ll take advantage of the more recent progress in upscaling and the like, perhaps to prevent the machine costing an absolute fortune?

This topic isn’t ignored. Describing it as a factor “the team couldn’t have foreseen when Project Helix began,” the component crisis gets a mention. “Meeting this challenge has become a primary driver of Helix’s innovation,” says the article. Ronald is quoted once more. “It’s definitely a challenging time, but as a system and a platform designer, it’s also one of the most exciting times because we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable.” This, he says, is why there’s the focus on neural rendering, adding, “I think you’re going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you’ve seen in the last 10 years.”

It’s all a lot of words to avoid pointing out that Microsoft itself is one of the primary causes of the crisis in the first place, one arm taking all the available components from the other in order to power its AI hubris.

Beyond this, the piece delivers some very confusing messaging regarding Xbox’s current desperate rebranding. After a disastrous attempt to call everything from your console to your toaster “an Xbox,” the recent emphasis has been to return to the core idea of the Xbox itself, yet that message gets very lost in Microsoft’s own marketing. We’re told at once that this is all about “the Return of Xboxâthe return of a console,” and then that “Project Helix aims to take a wrecking ball to the dividers currently keeping players and their games apart,” quoting Ronald saying Helix is about “enabling [players] to experience those games wherever they choose to play. It’s about removing barriers to play, removing friction, and those arbitrary boundaries that have existed in the past.” So which is it? There are claims the new UI will adapt to whether the Xbox is being played on the living room TV, or streamed to a mobile device or a PC with mouse and keyboard. This really does sound like a confusion of previous messaging crashing into the current reverse-ferret.

There’s no word one when we can expect to see Project Helix in more detail, and certainly nothing on an intended release date. It seems that Microsoft and Sony are currently playing chicken on revealing whether they’re aiming for 2027 or 2028, or perhaps even later given the tumult in the hardware industry. But at least we know it’s a console, not a PC, but also like a PC, and can be streamed to your mobile, or played on PC, and has all of the annoying complexity of PCs taken away, but also still there.

For the first time in eight years, Johnny Depp is back on top of the box office. Ebenezer is set to easily earn the most in theater grosses this weekend, and in doing so, it leads us all to a pretty obvious question. Is Johnny Depp back?

The Pirates Of The Caribbean lead was arguably the biggest movie star in the entire world for an extended period of time in the 2000s and 2010s before the fallout from his relationship with Amber Heard devolved into lawsuits, abuse allegations and tabloid headlines. Apart from the occasional artsy project here or there, he’s basically disappeared from theaters since Covid, but now, thanks to Ebenezer, he’s reminding everyone in Hollywood that he’s one of the most bankable stars on the planet.

You can take a look at the box office chart below, which has strong estimates thanks to some fine work over at The Numbers…

So, does this mean Johnny Depp is back? Well, the short answer is probably sort of, as some are predicting. The long answer is a little more complicated. Hollywood studios care about success more than any other metric, and there’s a lot of success here for Depp. Ebenezer was reportedly made for less than forty million dollars, and while critic reviews are middling, fan response has been terrific with an A- CinemaScore. The Hollywood Reporter claims half of the people who saw the movie this weekend cited Deep and his make-up heavy role as the primary reason they went, and Deadline further claims that the movie is putting people in seats across the entire country, not just in certain theaters that cater to certain demographics.

Add the positive word of mouth to the fact that it’s a holiday movie, and there’s every reason to believe Ebenezer will have a nice little extended run here in theaters. In short, it’s going to remind all of the executives and producers working in show business that Depp, despite his extended absence, is still one of the most bankable stars in all of Hollywood, even if we haven’t seen it since he was starring in the Fantastic Beasts franchise. He’s almost certainly going to get a few projects with elevated budgets coming out of this.

We already know one of those is for sure coming. Amazing Spider-Man director Marc Webb cast Depp in his next movie opposite Penelope Cruz called Day Drinker. That’s scheduled to hit theaters in March of 2027. I think it would be a surprise not to see him pick up commitments for a few more movies in the wake of this success too. I don’t think quite Marvel-style $250M event films, but I think they’ll be the type of projects that will get wide releases and have high upside. We’ll see though.

Outside of Depp, it was a pretty sleepy weekend at the box office. The Cat In The Hat held onto second place for its second consecutive weekend. It should continue doing solid business for at least a few more weeks as a great option for families. Godzilla Minus One fell quite a bit more, but that’s not a surprise for a foreign language film with a passionate target audience. The people who wanted to see that movie were always going to come out its first weekend, which is why it put up such a huge number en route to victory last weekend.

The story wasn’t quite as promising for some of the other new entries beyond Ebenezer. Ghost Soldier and How To Rob A Bank both struggled to find a wide audience and were barely able to top five million dollars. It’s unlikely either will be able to build off those disappointing numbers, but we’ll have to wait and see for next weekend when the latest edition of The Hunger Games looks poised to absolutely dominate in what could be a hundred million dollar money cannon.

#3724. Magic: The Gathering animated series Planeswalker is coming to Netflix in 2027

Netflix's long-gestating Magic: The Gathering animated series is called Planeswalker, and it's coming in 2027.

The title was revealed at MagicCon Atlanta, and Netflix shared a first look at the show on Twitter/X on 13th November. "Every great story begins with a spark. Here's your first look at Planeswalker, a new animated series based on Magic: The Gathering. Coming to Netflix in 2027", the company wrote, and shared a teaser, which you can see below:

According to a synopsis shared with IGN, the series follows Chandra Nalaar, "a volatile pyromancer hunted for her gifts, and haunted by her past". It continues: "Confronted by an insidious force, Chandra and some of the most legendary Planeswalkers must harness their extraordinary abilities, navigate treacherous alliances, and battle their own inner demons to prevent a cataclysmic war that threatens to consume their very existence".

Netflix first announced a Magic: The Gathering series in June 2019, with Avengers: Endgame directors Joe and Anthony Russo attached, and it was originally due in late 2022. Two years in, the original showrunners departed over creative differences, and in September 2024, Netflix confirmed it had started again from scratch with Star Trek: Picard and 12 Monkeys showrunner Terry Matalas in charge.

IGN reports that Matalas, who most recently ran Marvel's VisionQuest, is running the show alongside Cindy Appel. Budapest-based studio DIGIC Pictures is handling the animation.

At the end of last month, we learned PUBG is also being turned into a live-action series for Netflix, with Donald Glover set to direct, write, executive produce, and star.

Glover is a two-time Emmy and Golden Globe winner, best known for Atlanta and Community. Krafton calls PUBG "one of the world’s most enduring gaming franchises", and says the game, which is credited with popularising the battle royale genre, holds seven Guinness World Records.

"We’ve seen a lot of discussion about the (DPS) role of the season 6 hero. We understand that you were looking forward to another support hero next season and I hope that giving context for the decision will help players understand it, even as some of them are disappointed."

"When we started work on the detective, he was a support. But as time went on and the kit continued development we realized that it wasn’t working. Once we tested Hudson as a DPS, the turn around in our feelings for him was instantaneous and dramatic. This decision ultimately wasn't whether we release a DPS or a support hero, it was whether we release a great character or one we didn't believe in. Building heroes for OW is as much of an art form as a technical challenge." via a social media post.

Last week we found out a few new things about the next hero coming to Overwatch in season 6. He's an omnic detective, his name's Hudson, he has a fun accent, and he will be a DPS. Hudson is the last hero to be released from the batch teased earlier this year during Overwatch's Spotlight, and after all this time I'm very excited to see what he has to offer. But not everyone shares this sentiment.

There's a good chunk of players who are upset about Hudson, before they've even tried him out, simply because he's not a support hero, which was what Team 4 initially promised him to be. I've seen this discontent online and honestly ignored it, thinking it was either bots or people farming for attention because I cannot fathom why anyone is honestly upset about this.

I've been maining support in Overwatch for almost 10 years now, ever since open queue grinded me down and I accepted that no matter how much I liked DPS, I had to role fill if we wanted to win games. So, after all these years I love getting my hands on a new support hero, but after four new supports this year (including Sombra's transition to the role), I'm more than satisfied with the role's current diversity of heroes.

But Team 4 is taking the criticism seriously, as Keller has addressed it directly. Aside from trying to convince players that shoehorning a hero into a role just because that was the plan 10 months ago isn't a great idea, he also explains how "game dev isn't always straightforward" and how the team needs "to adapt to create the best version of something".

I completely agree. I'd much rather have a hero that was crafted for a role holistically than one forced into it to fill a quota. Letting the people who know Overwatch the best, aka the devs, have the freedom to craft heroes and change them when needs be is what will ensure the best possible outcome.

This is such a non-issue, especially considering how strong the support roster currently is. Look at our poor tank players for example, forced to switch between Orisa and Mauga every game. Go give them some love and attention, lord knows they need the energy much more than us over in support.

#3721. Jesen Huang Reportedly Goes From Calling Himself A ‘Piece Of Sh*t’ To Exploring A Return To Nvidia

The dust is still settling from Nvidia’s ousting of founder Jensen Huang over reports of multiple affairs, which allegedly involved two employees at the tech firm. Huang supporters have been apoplectic about the move, while shareholders are still trying to price in exactly what the scandals and Huang’s departure will mean for the company’s future. But what if Huang comes back?

Industry observers have likened such a possibility to when Steve Jobs left Apple and later returned, though he did so without the cloud of alleged Chinese spies and romantic relationships that violated company conduct standards hanging over his head. New reporting claims that Huang has been working with a crisis PR firm for nearly a year to try to do damage control on the inevitable outing of his relationship with Megaspeed associate Alice Huang. Did things go off-script or is this all part of a larger plan by Huang to not go as quietly as it may have first seemed?

Bloomberg recently reported that the current swirl of scandals had left the founder feeling “depleted.” He had allegedly even taken to making self-flagellating remarks. “Huangâs usual take-charge demeanor had evaporated, according to a person familiar with the situation, and heâd started using phrases like ‘whatever’ and ‘I donât care,'” it wrote. “I’m a piece of shit” was apparently another thing some heard him say at some point.

But The Financial Times now suggests Huang may be plotting an attempted return. It claims he recently spoke with confidants about the possibility of mounting a comeback at Nvidia. Some allies were even reportedly setting up a “war room” to work on selling that narrative to the company’s board and shareholders. More baseless speculation from randos in Huang’s orbit, or is it all a necessary part of the fall and rise crisis comms playbook the former CEO is running?

Nvidia is set to release its newest quarterly earnings this month, and those are expected to show another astronomical increase in year-over-year profits. The most shocking thing about this entire sordid AI ordeal is not that Huang allegedly had multiple affairs, but that Nvidia’s board was willing to dump the founder so quickly despite his public image and persona being so integral to the company’s underlying brand and recent meteoric success.

Huang basically took Nvidia from gaming graphics backwater to pillar of the global AI economy in just a few years thanks to being in the right place at the right time. Companies have fought much harder to protect much less.

#3720. Call of Duty Endowment marks Remembrance Day with veterans' Valor Pack push

The Call of Duty Endowment is marking Remembrance Day and its 17th anniversary by encouraging Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone players to pick up its Valor Pack, with all of Activision's net proceeds going towards helping veterans find jobs.

The Call of Duty Endowment Valor Pack - which has been available since Modern Warfare 4 launched on 23rd October - was designed by the Endowment and Infinity Ward with US Marine Corps veteran and Medal of Honor recipient Kyle Carpenter in mind.

The items include a melee weapon blueprint inscribed with "Worth Fighting For", plus items called Relentless and Still Standing.

According to the Call of Duty blog, 100 percent of Activision's net proceeds from the pack (after VAT and sales tax) go to the Endowment.

To mark Remembrance Day, players who owned it and launched either game before 6pm GMT on 12th November also received double XP tokens and a DMZ survival kit.

"Veterans bring incredible skills into the workplace after military service," said Carpenter.

The Endowment, which supports veterans in the UK as well as the US, says it has now helped place more than 180,000 into "high-quality jobs", and wants to reach 200,000 by 2030.

Other partners are also raising money, with Pilot's round-up campaign raising more than £4.7 million ($6 million) for the Endowment since 2019. Polaris will also donate around £19,500 ($25,000) if players collectively complete 5 million rides in its DAGOR vehicle across Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone by 25th November.

It comes two weeks after Activision apologised to bereaved families of the Itaewon crowd crush victims and confirmed it would remove real footage of the tragedy from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. Players discovered that the game's opening cinematic uses short news clips to depict fictional civilian casualties during a North Korean invasion of South Korea. Those clips have since been found to include archive footage from the 2022 Itaewon disaster, in which around 160 people died.

For years, Johnny Galecki was one of network television's biggest stars. His long-running sitcom, The Big Bang Theory was a hit, and hits bring fame and big paydays. Galecki could have taken his money and retired to a quiet life, and it turns out he wrestled with that decision between then and his latest gig as I just found out.

After seven years, Galecki is returning to acting by way of a theatrical production of Kowalski, and ahead of that, he talked to BroadwayWorld.com about why he chose this project. It's a fair question considering Big Bang spinoff series Stuart Fails to Save the Universe was part of the 2026 TV schedule, and I'm sure the creative team would've loved to have had him in Season 1. It turns out Galecki's decision to take this role was about more than just having a job, but wanting to see if he still had a passion for acting:

I knew I was in a position where I needed to learn if I still loved this work or not, honestly. I was beyond confused, I was concerned that this very first love of mine, and for a very long time my only love, seemed to have left me. And I was very content, but it was a bit of an identity crisis, I suppose. Or lack of knowing where I fit in the world, all of a sudden. I’d been doing theatre since I was seven and acting in various mediums since. And so, I just couldn’t figure it out, why I was entirely bereft of any interest in it any longer.

Galecki did indeed have options considering how much money he made from The Big Bang Theory. He reportedly makes a good deal more via reruns as well, so it's not like he needed to return to acting. And yet, as someone who has been working as an actor since childhood, it was a major part of his identity. Taking on this role was a test to see if he still loved being a performer, or if he needed to figure out what the next chapter of his life looked like.

And, with that, we now have him playing Tennessee Williams in Kowalski. It's not just a role, as Johnny Galecki pointed out, but one that will challenge his abilities as an actor:

I knew it needed to be something that would challenge me, something that I couldn’t hide behind, something that I couldn’t blame on it being underwritten, or a thankless role if it failed.

It's interesting to read that comment, and I do wonder if that's meant to be a pointed jab at what roles could've been waiting for him. It's easy to imagine that Stuart Fails to Save the Universe would love to bring in Johnny Galecki to reprise Leonard Hofstadter eventually, likely for one of the cameo roles we've seen others like Kaley Cuoco play. Is this a hint that co-creator Chuck Lorre shouldn't hold his breath about the Leonard actor reprising the role?

Should that be the case, he's not the only star with a stance on that. Sheldon Cooper actor Jim Parsons openly stated that he's done playing the character, which could put the Chuck Lorre series in a sticky situation. Stuart and friends need to find one of Leonard, Sheldon, or Howard to help set the universe right, and now it's looking like they may have to wait for a while.

All this to say, Johnny Galecki didn't openly besmirch his time working on Big Bang Theory. It's just hard not to think about that when it was the last role that he played before this big return to acting. It could be that this statement had nothing to do with his work on TBBT at all, but I can't help but wonder. Regardless of that, I'm glad he's found a role that he finds both challenging and exciting.

Catch episodes of TBBT by streaming them with an HBO Max subscription, or find them in syndication on various networks. Now that Johnny Galecki is acting again, I'll be curious to see if he starts to pick up more work! I guess it depends on how this acting stint goes.

Ashes of the Singularity 2 has some neat ideas for army management, but a poor campaign, an underwhelming new faction, and obtrusive generative AI use undermines the enterprise

PC Gamer's got your back Our experienced team dedicates many hours to every review, to really get to the heart of what matters most to you. Find out more about how we evaluate games and hardware.

What is it? RTS sequel in the lineage of Supreme Commander

Reviewed On: AMD Ryzen 5 3600, Nvidia 2080 Super, 32 GB RAM, Windows 10.

Ashes of the Singularity 2 can't be faulted for scale. Much like its predecessor, the RTS sequel delivers on the promise of letting players control truly colossal armies. Rolling up huge globs of units and tossing them at your enemy lines in a giant, explosion-riddled mud fight is never subtle and only occasionally clever. But for any veteran RTS player, watching miles-long lines of armies clash is inevitably going to stir the soul.

Unfortunately, scale is also the sum of what Ashes of the Singularity 2 offers. As a sequel, it does little to build on the strengths of the original, while largely failing to address that first game's weaknesses. The campaign is terrible, the story borderline incomprehensible, and the whole experience is overshadowed by the spectre of generative AI.

Before we get into Ashes 2's numerous problems, I do want to give Oxide Games credit for one thing: for a game of this scale, Ashes of the Singularity 2 is remarkably easy to control. In terms of base-building, Ashes of the Singularity 2 is a largely familiar RTS affair. You build your production buildings, your resource harvesters, your defensive structures, and that's more or less it.

When it comes to unit recruitment, however, Ashes 2 is much more interesting. While units are still recruited individually, they're also automatically assigned into armies at the recruitment phase. You build a new army by queueing up all the units you want, and then when you're done, you assign a rally point for the army on the map, and all the units will just assemble there.

Once recruited, armies can be selected with the number keys and controlled like a single unit, and they tend to move and attack pretty intuitively, although pathfinding does struggle with narrow passes or rough terrain (which, to be fair are both things that real armies struggle with). This makes it very easy to oversee multiple armies at once.

In addition, when in battle, you can replenish destroyed units at the press of a button, or simply set the army to reinforce automatically. It's another convenient touch, and encourages you to support your forces by constructing new production buildings close to the frontline.

It's not the only area where Ashes 2 displays an intuitive flourish. Alongside selecting the relevant structure from the menu, you can also construct harvester buildings directly from the resource node, while upgradeable buildings will often display an upgrade button over them that you can click. In terms of UI/UX design, Ashes 2 successfully minimises rooting through menus. Everything is accessible through shortcuts, directly on the screen, or a single menu layer.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

This system does come at the cost of some finer control. Unit recruitment is bottlenecked to one unit per production building type, no matter how many buildings of that type you have. This means building an army composed of specific units (such as aerial units) takes longer, so armies tend to take a similar shape. On the subject of aerial units, they are a bit of a weak point for Ashes 2. Not only are they easily countered by AA units and emplacements, they also don't match the speed of ground units when in a mixed army, with a tendency to fly off and get themselves obliterated. Regardless, army control is by far the best thing about Ashes 2.

The sequel does introduce some other new features, such as a new faction, the United Earth Forces; unfortunately it's the least interesting faction in the game.

The UEF is a deeply vanilla sci-fi army, composed of tanks, jets and human soldiers so tiny they get instantly lost once the match scales up. It's way less compelling than the many mechs of the Post-Human Coalition, or the robotic insects of the AI Substrate. Where the Substrate's dreadnought units include a giant squid that fires laser beams and a blimp that shoots swarms, the UEF gets a big tank and a knockoff Megazord. Granted, the tank functions as a mobile base. That's useful, but it isn't fun.

The UEF is also the sole focus of Ashes 2's campaign. This is disappointing, but it's also the least of the campaign's problems. It's composed of 10 missions, roughly half of which are rigid tutorials with passive AI that offers virtually no challenge whatsoever.

The second half, which takes place in locations across the solar system, is better. The missions actually play with Ashes 2's scale and gradually let the AI off the leash. Indeed, the final two missions offer some pretty fierce resistance. But despite being set in locations like the Moon and on a weaponised asteroid bound for earth, they're also unambitious, meat and potatoes scenarios with no real twists or turns.

The result is four, maybe five hours of half-decent campaigning, which just isn't good enough in 2026.

The result is four, maybe five hours of half-decent campaigning, which just isn't good enough in 2026. It highlights how generous and meticulous Tempest Rising's campaigns were, built around thrilling, rapidly changing scenarios that sought to stretch the player's skills.

It doesn't help that the story is dreadful—a three way philosophy and ethics lecture between humans, AI, and uploaded post-human personality constructs. It's a parade of characters you never actually see babbling endlessly about the vague machinations of AI threats and whether or not post-humans are still the same people they were when they were bags of flesh and juice.

Ironically, the story is also where Oxide's use of generative AI is most evident. According to Ashes 2's Steam AI disclosure, Oxide used AI to "provide post processing effects and animation to art created by human Stardock artists for some of the campaign cutscenes" while "some cutscenes use Stardock human artist-made 3D assets with AI to composite the final shot." Finally, "some in-game unit barks, notifications, and a few minor characters use pre-generated ElevenLabs stock voices".

Frankly, I'm skeptical that this represents the limit of Oxide's AI use. All the character portraits look straight up AI generated to me, and the voice lines sound similarly infected. AI or not, it's something of a moot point because, either way, they're both awful. The portraits have that horrible, plasticky AI sheen to them, while the acting is often weirdly intoned in a way that does not help the narrative's bamboozling quality.

What bugs me most about Ashes 2's AI use, though, is that the RTS genre has such a rich heritage in cinematic storytelling. Warcraft 3, StarCraft 2 and Homeworld all successfully balanced their sci-fi grandeur with intimately human tales. Command & Conquer, meanwhile, was one of the earliest PC games to directly put a human face on videogame storytelling. From Kane to Tanya to Tim Curry escaping to the one place that hasn't been corrupted by capitalism, C&C's FMVs are often the thing that players most fondly remember.

I understand that Oxide Games probably doesn't have a Tim Curry budget. But it also doesn't need it. C&C's FMVs aren't remembered because they're expensive, or even especially great storytelling. They're remembered because they're fun, silly, intensely human creations. You don't need a massive budget to replicate that. If Oxide Games stuck a beret on a programmer and had them ham it up in front of the camera, the result would be infinitely preferable to Ashes 2's airy, inhuman waffle.

With the campaign a write-off, you're left with multiplayer and skirmish mode. Skirmish is arguably where Ashes of the Singularity has always been at its strongest, and playing against the AI here is certainly better than the campaign, offering a wide range of difficulty levels that lets you find your own sweet-spot. Putting together a four-way grudge match, watching the scale of the conflict slowly build-out, commanding multiple armies on multiple fronts, you get a sense of what Ashes 2 could be.

Yet here too, there are problems. None of the maps particularly spark joy. It's a roster of generic biomes and moonscapes that offer little in the way of personality or artistic direction. Also—and this is a broader complaint—while I appreciate that Ashes 2 is meant to be a slow-burn affair, I think it is a little too slow overall. In particular, battles are too attrition-heavy, and beneath the visual fireworks, you don't necessarily feel the punch of your units in combat. When Dreadnought units clash, it should feel like two gods have descended from the heavens. Instead, it feels more like two giant snails squabbling over a particularly large leaf.

It's a shame, because the work Oxide has done to make such an unwieldy concept so, well, wieldy is impressive. Given more care and time (and less generative AI), I think this could have been a great RTS. But with the campaign such a bust, what you're paying for here is one new faction, a skirmish mode and multiplayer, and after 10 years, I just don't think that's sufficient for a sequel.

#3714. Ubisoft is reportedly making a new Rainbow Six Vegas game, nearly two decades after Vegas 2

Ubisoft is reportedly working on a new Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

According to Insider Gaming, the project is in early development at Ubisoft Montreal under the codename Spades. It’s one of three new projects reportedly in production at the studio, and sources suggest a second of those is also set in the Rainbow Six universe. Eurogamer hasn’t been able to verify the report.

It’s not yet clear what form the new game will take, but Insider Gaming’s sources said it's "likely Vegas 3 rather than a remake" of an existing game. Insider Gaming expects it will be several years before Ubisoft officially announces a new Vegas game.

Rainbow Six Vegas launched in 2006, followed by Rainbow Six Vegas 2 in 2008. Since then, the series has centred on 2015's Rainbow Six Siege, and in August, Ubisoft announced Rainbow Six Tactics, a single-player, turn-based spin-off from Ubisoft Paris due in 2027.

Rainbow Six now sits under Vantage Studios, the Ubisoft subsidiary set up last year that also oversees Assassin’s Creed and Far Cry, and in which Tencent holds a 26.32 percent stake.

Last week, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on two new Assassin's Creed games: one set in ancient Rome, and a mobile spin-off set in Jerusalem. The leak came less than a week after Ubisoft issued a statement about the future of the Assassin's Creed series, insisting there are currently no new remakes of the series' past games in the works.

For a number of families, the Christmas Season is all about Santa Claus and his gift-giving, but in Hollywood, Santa comes in the shape of Tom Cruise and his famous Christmas cake. Even Oprah Winfrey spends the holiday season waiting around for the legendary coconut cake to arrive on her doorstep. However, that seems to be changing this year now that Oprah has discovered the cake isn’t as exclusive as she thought.

That’s right: the Queen of Favorite Things and one of the most influential pop culture figures in the world used to wait all year for the infamous cake, just like Top Gun: Maverick co-star Glen Powell, longtime cake recipient Kristen Dunst, and, most recently, Digger scene partner Riz Ahmed. It’s hard to imagine any celebrity sitting around waiting for a cake to be delivered to them, especially Oprah, who has the ability to get whatever she wants. Yet that’s how all these stars have been spending their holiday season for several decades. Winfrey recently said:

In our house, we’d be like ‘Has the Tom Cruise cake come yet? Has the Tom Cruise cake come?’ And all these years, up until this year, I thought that Tom had the cake specially made for Tom, okay. Then I realized Tom has a bakery.

Now, I don’t think anyone thought Cruise was baking the Christmas coconut cakes himself. While he’s a talented actor and impressive stuntman, baking is time-consuming, and his schedule is usually packed. The identity of the bakery that prepares the cakes isn't a total secret, but now, Oprah has let that cat out of the bag on a grand scale.

During a podcast taping (shared on Instagram) where she had several caregivers in attendance, Winfrey revealed that Doan’s Family Bakery in Los Angeles was the one responsible for the Hollywood Christmas tradition and that anyone, including us normal people, can order the cake.

The Emmy-Award-winning host rejoiced at being able to order the cake whenever she wants. And in true Oprah fashion, her first instinct was to share the good news with those in her life:

I can get the cake! And so I started sending it to people, saying, ‘It’s the Tom Cruise cake.’

I'm wondering how Cruise will feel knowing that Winfrey has further emphasized the source of his famous gift With this, might he consider changing up his yuletide tradition and switch to something? It's hard to say, but even if he did, I'm sure he'd think of something just as special. After all, the Mission Impossible star is known for his generosity, like never forgetting to call Rosie O’Donnell for her birthday.

Winfrey shares the same generosity gene with Cruise, of course, so it’s no surprise that she instantly felt the need to share the cake with not only her friends and family, but also the caregivers in attendance for the podcast taping. Yep, everyone in the audience was promised a delicious coconut cake would be delivered to their door courtesy of Goldbelly. Check out the full clip below:

A post shared by The Oprah Podcast (@oprahpodcast)

I would be insanely jealous, but of course, the good news is that anyone can order the cake from Goldbelly right now. It’s not exactly cheap, but it might be worth it to say that I’ve tried the infamous “Tom Cruise Cake,” thanks to Oprah.

World of Warcraft: Forever's having some teething issues with its new spellcaster itemisation. The idea, to sum it up quick, is that a lot of the power that was in spells innately has been pushed onto items, instead, with the intention to make it feel really good when you get a cool new staff as a mage, for instance.

This has had unintended consequences, as discovered by Rextroy (the same madlad who solos raid bosses), as shared on YouTube. The problem is this: Gear in Forever can give a lot of raw power to your healing and damage spells, as part of the aforementioned changes. But that raw power also applies to lower-level healing spells, too.

In Forever (and in Classic), casting lower-level spells is a core part of managing your mana as a healer. In this instance, however, "the healing coefficient on healing power remains the same, which is around 43% [on a low level Flash of Light], so if I stack all healing green items, I get my healing power up towards 242," Rextroy explains.

This, combined with the Paladin talent Oath of Light (which slaps another 61 healing onto Flash of Light), along with Spiritual Focus and Concentration Aura, which makes it almost impossible for enemies to interrupt or push-back the casting of his Flash of Light, and this makes his paladin basically unkillable.

The low-rank version of his Flash of Light spell doesn't cost enough mana to outpace his natural mana regeneration, it heals for a bunch because of his gear, and enemies can't slow or interrupt it. Which makes him almost unkillable.

I say almost, because as his experimentations prove, he can still become stunned or crowd-controlled by high-level enemies. And there are limitations. While he can stand up to a level 60 enemy whacking on him, add two or three to the mix and he can no longer outpace their damage.

However, Rextroy finds a level 60 enemy he can kill, an abomination in Eastern Plaguelands, which he pulls using a bug that casts Echoes of Lordaeron, an anti-undead damage boost given to whichever faction controls the most towers in the zone, on enemies when he resurrects.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

And sure, it takes 20 minutes. And sure, he can only kill it because the abomination has almost zero surprises, extra attacks, or abilities to stun him. But he still does it, getting a whopping… uh, 468 experience points for his trouble.

Perhaps the more game-breaking result of this build, then, is the fact that he can use it to out-pace fatigue damage, which generally stops players from swimming way out into the ocean. This lets him access a non-instanced version of the Drowned City dungeon, which is visible off the coast of Stranglethorn but cannot be visited outside of the dungeon without sleeping with the fishes.

While I think the extent of this build is probably something that'll get adjusted or patched out, I do sort of hope the spirit of it is kept the same—part of the promise of Forever was that weird item combinations or cool builds would emerge out of the woodwork and let folks do niche, but powerful things.

Perhaps it's not great that Rextroy can both tank and heal a dungeon with this setup at the same time, but I'd still like it to work in some capacity.

#3707. Blade Runner 2099 bosses hint at a possible "triple-A" Blade Runner game in the future - just don't expect it any time soon

Blade Runner 2099 - an upcoming TV miniseries coming to Amazon Prime Video, acting as a sequel to Blade Runner (1982) and Blade Runner 2049 (2017) - might be getting a video game. And a 'triple-A' video game, at that. At least that's according to Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, executive producers for Blade Runner 2099 and co-CEOs of Alcon Entertainment (which owns the Blade Runner IP).

In a new interview with IGN, the duo reveal that they had thought about adapting the Blade Runner fracnhise into a game, and that - should it come to fruition - it would target "triple-A" in scope. Other than that, the duo seemed to want to keep any potential information to themselves. Given they appear to be in talks about the title, rather than in any active development, if something did come of this ideation, it would no doubt be a long, long way off. Kosove and Johnson's aim seems to be getting players to "interact" more with the world of Blade Runner, which has recently been fleshed out by the 2017 movie and is set to be developed more in the upcoming series.

Of course, we've seen Blade Runner games before. There was 1997's simply-titled Blade Runner - developed by Westwood Studios and published by Virgin Interactive - which was a point-and-click adventure that really seemed to pick up the vibes the original Ridley Scott was putting down. An Enhanced Edition of the game was released in 2022, which is actually more of a remake than a simple enhancement.

Then, in 2023, Annapurna Interactive unveiled its very first internally-developed game, in the form of Blade Runner 2033: Labyrinth. The game, which promised to riff on the dystopian universe established in Ridley Scott's cult classic movie, would have been sandwiched squarely between that film and its sequel, Blade Runner 2049. It was going to be set in LA after the Blackout hits, but beyond that - and the fact it's coming to PC and consoles at some point - few details ever managed to break through the PR barrier before the game went dark: it's been removed from Annapurna's website and delisted from Steam. Curious.

If you want to see something more from the cyberpunk world sooner, Blade Runner 2099 releases on Prime Video on 25th November.

#3705. People Said Daniel Radcliffe Was ‘F--ked’ After Harry Potter. How He Succeeded Anyway

The Harry Potter film series may have ended in 2011, but its lead, Daniel Radcliffe, remains a household name. He’s made a splash not only by taking on so many “weird” film projects, but he's also made a mark in TV and on Broadway. If you can believe it, the British actor himself said people told him he would have career troubles after his Wizarding World days. However, Radcliffe ultimately succeeded, and he recently recalled how all that happened..

After Daniel Radcliffe nailed his adorable, precious Harry Potter audition when he was 11, his life would change forever. However, the David Copperfield actor opened on The Old Man and the Three about how challenging it was for him in transitioning to life post-Potter. And I didn’t expect such a brutally honest take:

The thing I always say about Potter and what it did for me in terms of like — towards the end of the films I started getting all of us started getting the question a lot from journalists of like, ‘What are you going to do after this?’.... The implication was always like, ‘Well, you're fucked now aren't you? What are you going to do after this? There's nothing left.’ And you know, actually as I look back and I'm like, I can't believe people were saying that kind of stuff to a teenager. It's a really crazy thing to say to a young person.

It's a real shame that people suggested that to Radcliffe and put so much pressure on him at a young age. From the outside looking in, it almost seemed like he was being set up to fail. I can understand that there are many actors out there who are forever remembered for one role. However, that didn't necessarily mean the December Boys actor would be one of them. Radcliffe continued to explain on the podcast that he didn’t let anyone’s negativity bother him:

So I think there's a thing that happens when part of growing up famous is that as you are trying to figure out who you are, you are getting this perceived version of yourself reflected back at you from like a million places and a million people all the time. And so you have to figure out what of that is not real and what you actually are and what you actually want.

After Radcliffe spent so many years playing The Boy Who Lived, I can really understand why he'd go down a path of self-discovery. Even his Harry Potter co-star, Alan Rickman, advised him and other alumni to try theater. And lo and behold, Radcliffe would eventually star in the Broadway show Merrily We Roll Along, which made tons of money and landed him his first Tony Award.

Plus, we can’t forget that Radcliffe got into “deeply fucking weird” stuff in film projects that would come after Potter. To name a few examples, he played a farting corpse in Swiss Army Man, sported pistols for hands in Guns Akimbo, and showed his dark side while growing horns from his head in, well, Horns. Plus, we can’t forget when he put the weird in Weird: The Al Yankovic, which he described as his favorite film he did post-Potter.

It goes without saying that Daniel Radcliffe has been quite fortunate, and he can openly admit he hasn't done it alone. He also credits the creatives he's worked with for hiring him:

So a lot of people were asking us like, ‘What are you going to do after this, and are you going to be typecast?’ And I think there has — I'm sure there is an element of there are some directors out there who particularly in the first few years after Potter didn't want me in their movie because they're like, ‘Everyone will just be seeing Harry Potter when they look at him.’ But for every one of those directors, there was also a director that went, ‘Oh, I would like him in my movie because I want to be the person that reinvents him or that can show an audience this actor that they think they know in a different light.’

Well, there you go. It appears that directors wanted the credit to be able to help show Radcliffe’s versatility outside of playing a wizard. Of course, many filmmakers naturally become impressed when an actor knows how to step outside of his comfort zone and take on different roles. To that point, Radcliffe’s former Harry Potter director, Chris Columbus, was definitely impressed with the talented actor’s career moves when the franchise ended, saying his projects showed how “fearless” he was.

Even though Radcliffe received a lot of negativity that his career would end once Harry Potter did, I’m so happy they were proven wrong. And, with that, the public at large has been able to enjoy watching the actor take on a plethora of roles. While the fantasy franchise will always be a career-defining moment, I’m glad that Radcliffe is thriving and continuing to test himself as an actor.

Fans can still revisit the films that first brought fame to the English actor, though as the Harry Potter movies are streaming now with an HBO Max subscription. And don’t forget that the book-adapted TV series will head arrive on that same streamer as part of the streaming schedule on Christmas Day.

Just your average South Floridian cinephile who believes the pen is mightier than the sword.

#3704. Treyarch lays off lead Call of Duty writer and Zombies veteran after "approximately 20 years" of service

"Thanks to all the fans for your enthusiasm, support, and kind words over the years."

Treyarch's former Senior lead writer, Craig Houston, has been laid off after approximately 20 years of service with the developer. In a post made to both his Twitter/X account and LinkedIn, the developer thanked fans for their support during his two decades with the company and confirmed he was impacted by recent reorganistation within the studio.

"After approximately 20 years, I was sadly one of those affected by recent layoffs," he noted in his posts. "I am proud to have worked with so many talented people - many of whom will remain friends for life. Thanks to all the fans for your enthusiasm, support, and kind words over the years."

On Twitter/X, he quote tweeted a video celebrating 30 years of Treyarch and featuring footage from many of the games he worked on to share his message. It appears the layoffs referenced are part of the broad reorganistation affecting 3200 jobs that Xbox announced earlier this year. Treyarch, as part of Activision Blizzard, is owned by Xbox.

Houston is a bonafide veteran of the esteemed FPS series. His first Call of Duty title at Treyarch was Call of Duty 3, where he worked as a video editor. This was followed by World at War, Black Ops 1 through 4, where he is credited as a writer and designer. For Modern Warfare, Black Ops - Cold War, Vanguard, Modern Warfare 3, then Black Ops 6 and 7, he is listed as a member of the design team and in 'creative development'. He is not credited on this year's Modern Warfare 4.

If you've picked up a Call of Duty game in the past decade-plus, you'll have interacted with Houston's work: he was a central creative force behind the writing for Treyarch's campaign modes since 2006 (with Call of Duty 3) and the main writer for the Zombies mode since 2008 (with Call of Duty: World at War). Alongside Jimmy Zielinski, Jason Blundell, and Kevin Drew, Houston was an integral part of the evolution of the Zombies pillar of Call of Duty, and shaped it into the series-defining thing it is today. There has been a fair amount of community support for Houston since he announced the news yesterday; he was a popular dev, and a lot of the Zombies-specific fan communities online hold a lot of respect for him.

"Craig is a great guy," notes one user on Reddit. "You can tell how much he loves the story/characters he writes just by how excited he is when he talks about them in promo material."

"You're a Legend Craig, it was an honor to work with you," says ex-Treyarch vet, Tony Flame, in a reply to Houston's X post. "You created a truly special experience that will live on in the kinds of millions fans. Wishing you the best [...]."

From all of us here at Eurogamer, and myself personally - who really admires the character-work and emergent storytelling present in the Xbox 360-era Call of Duty games, specifically - we wish you the best and good luck with the future, Craig.

#3703. ‘Actively Makes The Game Worse’: Fans Are Furious With Pikmin 4′s Paid Nintendo Switch 2 ‘Upgrade’

Last Thursday, Pikmin 4 finally received its Nintendo Switch 2 Edition upgrade, promised to add improved visuals, voice commands for the adorable Oatchi, and a new set of bonus levels in the added “Dandori Academy.” But rather than serve as an incentive for Pikmin lovers to return to the game over the weekend, it looks like it’s mostly just pissed off people who paid the $10 for what they say barely qualifies as an upgrade.

Updated this graphic again now that Dandori Academy is out and… ðð

At least XDE isn't alone anymore https://t.co/2ZGYyqrcuE pic.twitter.com/B9tsSXziSb

— Shifted Pyro (@ShiftedPyro) November 15, 2026

At the time I’m writing this, Pikmin 4 Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy (to use its full, Christian name) has a 2.1 user score on Metacritic out of 265 ratings. While 265 isn’t a huge amount of user reviews, that is a remarkably low score for a game that has a base version sitting comfortably at 8.9. And the comments are full of the same, repeated complaints: framerates are still at 30 FPS, loading screens now take longer than they did in the original, and the new content is mostly a bunch of reused maps from the base game that can only be played at certain times.

“charging customers for almost no content nor technical enhancements (in fact, load times are even longer on NSW2 – itâs a disgrace!)” reads a 0/10 review from laurack.

“This is essentially a paid downgrade and calling this is a ‘lazy Switch 2 Edition’ or a ‘waste of money’ is an understatement for what is supposed to be an upgrade,” writes PrestonandTom in a 1/10 review. “This ‘upgrade’ of Pikmin 4 somehow manages to make the game run significantly worse with standard load times going from 6 seconds to 30+ seconds. The framerate went from an consistent 30 FPS to an inconsistent 30 FPS. Even despite all these problems, the new content isn’t that fun or engaging for the player by offering weak rewards for getting good dandori scores. The resolution is higher, but the tradeoff is not worth it and neither is the ‘new’ dandori academy content which mostly consists of old dandori levels that are already available in the base game.”

“While Pikmin 4 remains the undisputed peak of the franchise, this ‘Switch 2 Edition’ is a tough sell for returning veterans,” writes marcoskalil in a 7/10 review. “The bump in resolution and draw distance is welcome, but it ultimately highlights older textures that haven’t been properly upscaled for the new hardware. The bonus mode offers genuinely fun, meaningful content for long-time fans, yet it falls short of justifying the upgrade price. If you missed the original launch, this is undeniably the definitive way to play. However, if you have already conquered PNF-404 on the base Switch and is looking for more quality Olimar adventures, keep your Pikmin planted and hold out for Pikmin 5.”

“Very disaster edition game scam man!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!” wrote Lolitroppotsund in a succinct 0/10 review.

There are also a handful of criticisms, both there and in other communities, of the big Dandori Academy banner taking up space on this edition’s menu screen:

Bruh , Pikmin 4 nintendo switch 2 edition title screen is so ugly byu/Independent-Week-463 inPikmin

Now, not everyone is convinced the upgrade is horrible. Over on the Pikmin subreddit, longtime franchise fans are rolling their eyes a bit at the metascores, suggesting they’re “overdramatic” and that the release is in line with some of Nintendo’s other Switch 2 Edition upgrades. That said, not an awful lot of people are actively popping up in strong defense of the new edition, instead mostly just insisting it’s not as bad as the score suggest.

is it really that bad? byu/Papanataaa inPikmin

I’ve been holding off on playing Pikmin 4 for this update, but now I’m left questioning whether or not I ought to just save myself some money and buy the regular edition. The fans are right that it’s not the end of the world, and admittedly Nintendo didn’t promise much. But it is still a paid upgrade that, in at least one respect, makes the original game worse, and doesn’t seem to add much meaningful to balance that out. Pick it up at your own risk.

Final Fantasy 14 is set to make some big changes when the upcoming expansion Evercold releases in February. An overhaul to combat, dailies, and new raid difficulties are set to shake things up and, hopefully, keep people sticking around for longer.

And judging by a recent Letter from the Producer, Naoki Yoshida really wants folks coming back to see what Evercold is all about. So much so that the game's offering 30 free days for long-gone adventurers… or a quick-and-dirty paid skip if you're so inclined.

"Encouraging players to return is no mean feat," Yoshida wrote. "People pause their adventures for all kinds of reasons, including dissatisfaction and loss of interest. Although we continually update the game to address such issues, the fact remains that getting players to resume their journey is a difficult task indeed."

I can only assume that for that reason, the decision's been made to offer up a $9 cash shop item that'll skip you through Endwalker's patch story, as well as all of Dawntrail up until the final story patch. Now Final Fantasy 14 has offered paid story skips in the past—it still does—but this is the first time it's explicitly offered one for the current expansion. Usually the skips'll stop dead before the current expansion, meaning you still need to play through the newest story.

It's a pretty niche paid skip, too. You'll need to have at least completed Endwalker's main story and have a level 90 job on your chosen character, and even then you'll still have to level up to 100 in your own time in order to tackle the final patch quest of Dawntrail. But worry not, if you haven't played the game in six months, you'll be able to snap up 30 days of free game time until January 14. Plenty of time to get a job to max level and prepare for Evercold.

I'm mostly surprised by the introduction of this paid item because Yoshida has long been rather protective of the game's story. Something he admits in this very same letter: "I strongly believe that FF14 is a story-driven MMORPG," he wrote. "On top of that, skipping it all means you likely won't be familiar with the battle system and therefore will become a burden for other players in multiplayer content."

I do find it a little funny that Yoshida is worried that story skippers will weigh others down in dungeons and the like—I've played many a level 100 dungeon with folks who have clearly played enough to understand how to play yet still can't press their buttons properly.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

But anyway, Yoshida does admit that there is a lot of story to get through. "The Hydaelyn and Zodiark saga alone encompasses five expansions' worth of content," he wrote. "And with Dawntrail marking the start of the second saga, plus the coming addition of Evercold, the story continues to unfold into something even larger."

It really does feel like Square Enix wants Evercold to mark a big resurgence for the game, one I really do hope pays off for the developer. I've been playing off-and-on since A Realm Reborn and have seen just about every evolution the game has taken, and also the ways it has stagnated over time. Its confidence in trying to draw people back has me excited for the changes that are coming.

As Sydney Sweeney continues to generate buzz due to her acting career, buzzy lingerie line, those splashy ads and more business ventures, there’s been a continued focus on her personal life. That includes her relationship with Scooter Braun, who has reportedly been helping her make career decisions. As rumors continue to swirl around their relationship, it’s been alleged that Sweeney wants to move to the UK. Now, there’s apparently more evidence that she’s planning a move like Meghan Markle and Prince Harry’s.

Not only has it been alleged that the Euphoria alum is looking for a new residence in the UK, and this claim has sparked a bit of speculation. A recent report from The Sun sheds more light on the purported matter and, according to the outlet, Sweeney recently viewed a property in the village of Little Tew. Per a source, the actress has allegedly informed her people in her inner circle that she’s aiming to split her time between the UK and her multiple properties in the United States. A source for the tabloid also said this:

Sydney has ­visited the Cotswolds twice in the past ten months, and absolutely loves it. She viewed property there within the past three months.

If Sweeney were to make the move, she would actually become just another one of the famous people who live in the area. Among the celebrities who live in the area are David and Victoria Beckham, Ellen DeGeneres and her wife, Portia de Rossi (whose house was thought to have flooded in 2024) and Jeremy Clarkson. The Sun’s insider went on to allege that due to the presence of multiple stars, Sweeney wouldn’t have to worry about residents making a fuss over her, and there’s apparently another benefit:

She doesn’t get bothered by locals, who are all well-used to seeing A-listers, and finds village life incredibly cute and quaint. It’s also a huge change of pace from LA and all the vultures circling. And she can lead a more peaceful life in the countryside. Pinewood Studios are also only about an hour away, meaning she could easily stay at home while filming should she land the gig.

This should all be taken with a grain of salt, considering that no one from Sydney Sweeney’s camp has confirmed or denied that she’s planning to make a new home across the pond. Still, this news comes at an interesting time, considering what’s been going on with the Duke and Duchess of Sussex as of late.

It was reported this past August that Markle and Prince Harry were moving back to the UK alongside their two kids, Archie and Lilibet. For the past six years, the pair lived in Montecito, California, as they relocated to the state after stepping back from roles as senior members of the British Royal Family. Harry and Markle reportedly used a private jet to return to the UK, and the trip allegedly cost them $120,000 in total.

Since returning to the country, the Duke and Duchess’ family has reportedly stayed with friends in the aforementioned Cotswolds. Earlier this month, though, it was reported that the pair had already slightly relocated. Apparently Markle, Harry and their brood moved to the “main house” on the estate after having lived in a “property on the estate.” As for the couple’s attempts to find a place of their own, it’s been alleged that their search has been stalled due to their “champagne tastes” purportedly not matching their financial portfolio.

The public at large will just have to wait and see whether the Duke and Duchess manage to land on a new property in the Cotswolds or somewhere else in the UK. In the meantime, those interested in updates on Sydney Sweeney may continue to watch for any further evidence of a reported move.

#3698. Cyberpunk 2077 mod Torrent adds 3D rain, lightning storms, and tyre spray to Night City

A new Cyberpunk 2077 mod has overhauled Night City's rain, swapping the game's flat wet weather effects for individual 3D drops and adding lightning storms.

As spotted by DSOGaming, modder CyanideX's mod, Torrent, gives each raindrop its own size and falling speed. The drops also react to the player's movement, so they stream towards the windscreen when you're driving fast. If you find the wind has picked up, blustery weather can also push them sideways, too.

The rain also catches the light from street lamps, neon signs, car headlights, and taillights, and won't fall through roofs or inside buildings. Drops splash on the ground, heavy rain leaves mist in the distance, and cars throw up spray from their tyres on wet roads.

The mod complements this with a new lightning system, with branching bolts that flash and flicker before fading, and that can arrive in bursts during heavier storms.

If you like a little lightning, the frequency of bolts can be adjusted across 10 levels, and with the AudioXL mod installed, thunder follows each strike, timed to how far away it landed.

For players sensitive to flashing lights, a Reduce Flashes option dims the lightning, replaces its flicker with a single slow glow, and halves the number of strikes.

Torrent supports Nova City 2 and other weather mods, and adds extra storm effects for Nova City 2 players, including mist that rolls through the streets with the wind. It’s available now on Nexus Mods.

#3696. The World’s Favorite Fanfiction Website Has Finally Returned After A Hack Took It Down For Weeks

Readers rejoice, Archive of Our Own has returned. The Organization for Transformative Works (OTW) has announced that the popular fanfiction website has been restored after a security incident late last month required it be taken down for emergency maintenance.

[update] Identified: AO3 is now up! Some features have been temporarily disabled to allow us to bring the site back earlier than the four-week mark. At this time, icons across the site (user icons, collection icons, etc.) are disabled, external work importing is unavaila…

— AO3 Status (@status.archiveofourown.org) 2026-11-15T08:28:56.090Z

Instead of the four weeks that were projected, the outage lasted roughly two, with the site coming back in time for folks preparing for the Thanksgiving holiday break, but possibly not soon enough for authors hoping to bank some work. In the site’s absence, several AI-slop-powered imitators popped up, composed of fics scraped from the site before its shutdown. One such site offered to “pay” authors royalties from purchases of AI-generated audiobooks of their fanfics. After a massive outcry that included alerting OTW of possible copyright infringement, the site was shut down.

The shutdown galvanized online fan communities, many of which resorted to sharing databases of downloaded fics to tide readers over until AO3 could come back. But such emergency fandom measures were themselves the source of discussion and debate concerning the ethics of redistributing fandom works outside of protected spaces like AO3, potentially without authorial consent and in defiance of the etiquette that generally exists between people who write fic and those who read it.

Those discussions aren’t going anywhere, but they may take a backseat now that AO3, like Aragorn busting through the gates of Helm’s Deep, has returned. Some features, including the ability to download fics in specific e-reader formats, are still disabled for now and OTW reports that the site may respond more slowly than normal due to everybody and their mom rushing back to get to their Heated Rivalry fics.

A mini PC with Intel's G3 chip would rock, but alas, we're left with just four Xe3 cores instead.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Motherboard manufacturer Biostar has just announced the BIPTL-IHT, a mini motherboard complete with an integrated Panther Lake-H processor. It's the first desktop Panther Lake motherboard to be released in retail.

As spotted by VideoCardz, the motherboard range has support for up to 128 GB of DDR-7200 MHz SO-DIMM memory and can come with the following chips:

All of these chips come with Xe3 graphics with four Xe cores, and are lacking the punchy integrated B390 iGPU (and its 12 Xe3 cores) that some mobile Panther Lake chips have. You can still do some light gaming on these integrated graphics, but you won't be making yourself a mini gaming PC with Biostar's latest.

Instead, it seems like the purpose of this motherboard is to support industrial PCs, but given Xe3 graphics support hardware-accelerated AV1 encoding and decoding, one could feasibly use the motherboard in a mini media server PC instead.

You are getting two M.2 Key-M slots here, with PCIe 5.0 x4 and PCIe 4.0 x2 connections. This allows for NVMe storage, and the memory is dual-channel too. You also get two HDMI ports, two DisplayPort 1.4 ports, and the motherboard can support up to four displays at once.

As it's a 'Thin' Mini-ITX motherboard, its dimensions are 170 mm by 170 mm. That's very small. We don't yet have a release date or price point for this motherboard range.

Still, it's a bit of a shame we don't have any mini motherboards with gaming-worthy integrated Panther Lake mobile chips yet. Especially as GPU prices are so high. I managed to get the chance to test out the Intel G3 Extreme in the Acer Predator Atlas 8 handheld, and it's pretty incredible for a chip with integrated graphics. It rocks both gaming and productivity tasks, given the size and heat.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

If it's good enough for gaming laptops, I'd say it's good enough for an itty bitty PC to hook up to your TV. Let's hope we don't have to wait too long for a motherboard with one of those in.
